message.reasoning:
We need to evaluate the student submission against rubric criteria C1-C4 and requirements R1-R15.

Let's go through each.

C1: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Requirements: what is primary mission, why needed, how many spacecraft and why, who are users.

The introduction describes coral reef monitoring, Great Barrier Reef, fluid lensing, ZYZZsat. It says only one satellite is required and why (no constant coverage needed, simplicity, cost, build time). Users: governmental and science agencies (CSIRO, BOM), funding by university/government. It references literature. It is fairly detailed. However, primary mission statement: "The spacecraft is intended to image and send data to ground stations for collation and analysis." It does say "Earth observation satellite – specifically for coral reef and ocean monitoring" in exec summary. In introduction: "The proposed satellite ‘ZYZZsat’" carries fluid lensing. It identifies need. Users are somewhat described. Overall high standard but maybe could be more explicit on operator/customers. Still likely Accomplished, maybe 8.

C2: Main body: mission design. Requirements: launch site/vehicle and why; orbit type and elements; manoeuvres; ground control facilities; communication frequency; mission duration/EOL; software/hand calcs, screenshots/files.

The report covers launch: Vega E from Guiana Space Centre, explains piggyback, why (equator, allied countries, etc.). Orbit: SSO at 600 km, inclination 97.79°, COE table, J2 perturbation, RAAN, argument of latitude. Some issues: RAAN 27.33° "indicates location of launch facility" is wrong - RAAN is not launch site location. Inclination 97.79 vs formula? For 600 km, SSO inclination ~97.79° is about right. Semi-major axis 6971 km correct. They mention circular, e=0. They discuss orbital manoeuvres: only EOL, no other. Ground control: Mt Pleasant Radio Observatory, Tasmania, STK access report, average ~10 min, frequent passes. Mission duration 5 years, EOL: drag sail, uncontrolled deorbit, graveyard orbit discussed. Screenshots: STK 3D views, ground tracks, access table, inclination vs altitude plot (hand calc likely). Software files? Deliverable requires STK files included; not evident in text. They mention STK simulations run but no files attached in report (maybe not shown). The requirement says include relevant screenshots and software files. They included screenshots but no software files in text. Could be in appendix? Not present. So partial.

Technical issues: Launch vehicle Vega E not yet built; they acknowledge. They select 2025 launch. Good. Orbit: SSO RAAN rate: 360°/year = ~0.9856°/day, they say 1°/day. Fine. They say "constant supply of sunlight to satellite will be captured by solar panels" - for SSO, yes, mostly sunlit. But they also say recording only in descending part, which is daytime? For a 10:30 AM descending node? Actually SSO with 600 km; not specified local time. They mention "descending part of its orbit" for daytime recording. Some confusion: descending node in sun-synchronous orbit could be morning or afternoon depending on RAAN. They say "DN path for orbits 1-15" and "where satellite is constantly in sunlight". For a sun-synchronous orbit, the entire orbit is not in sunlight, but the orbital plane maintains a constant angle to sun; the satellite still experiences eclipse periods. They incorrectly claim "constantly in sunlight" for descending path? Actually a sun-synchronous orbit has eclipse seasons; not constantly sunlit. Maybe they mean the descending passes are in daylight. But the ground track image shows descending node over Australia at 22:03 UTC, which is nighttime local? Hmm. Might be an error.

Also they say "a very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" - likely typo, should be "not desirable". But context says selecting altitude trade-off. It says "which is also desirable" - this is contradictory. Probably an error.

They say "The swath required for the satellite to cover the reef’s entirety would require either the sensor to swing or a very high altitude." Good. They choose 600 km but don't compute swath or resolution, no sensor specs. Lack of hand calculations for coverage/resolution. Some hand calc for inclination vs altitude plot.

They don't explicitly mention launch vehicle payload capacity, cost, or exact launch date.

They don't provide orbital manoeuvres for launch injection errors or station-keeping; only EOL. Requirement "Will you need to perform any orbital manoeuvres?" They say only at EOL. But for SSO maintenance, some station-keeping may be needed, though drag sail at EOL. They didn't discuss orbit maintenance (altitude decay due to drag at 600 km is small but over 5 years). Could be acceptable.

Communication: access table from STK. They report average 580.8 s (~9.7 min) and total 8711 s over 3 days? Wait table: first 15 accesses over Feb 3-5. Total duration 8711.797 s over about 3 days; that's ~48 minutes per day. They say "average contact duration of almost ten minutes" and "frequent amount of passes". They don't explicitly state how often (e.g., number of passes per day). The table shows 15 accesses over ~3 days = 5 per day. But they don't summarize frequency explicitly. Could infer. Requirement "how often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control?" They don't state number per day clearly. They say "already frequent amount of passes" but not explicit. Partial.

EOL: drag sail is reasonable; they mention no thrusters, passive. Good.

Software: STK screenshots, access report. No software files. Hand calc for inclination vs altitude. That's adequate.

C2 level: Likely Adequate to Accomplished. The design covers all major requirements but with some errors and missing details (no explicit communication frequency, no software files, some technical inaccuracies). Could be Adequate 6 or Accomplished 7. Given the depth, I'd say Adequate high (6) or Accomplished low (7). The rubric Accomplished requires "Major requirements are all addressed and well supported with quality evidence." Here some are missing (communication frequency, software files). So not all. Adequate: "Major requirements are addressed but may lack some detail or are not well supported with evidence." That fits. So C2 Adequate, maybe 6.

C3: Conclusion. It summarizes launch vehicle, orbit, ground station, mission purpose. It acknowledges Vega E not built yet. It is somewhat generic but does reach conclusions from evidence. Not very detailed. Adequate 5-6. Maybe 5.

C4: Report presentation. Structure: Executive summary, contents, introduction, mission design with subsections (Launch, Orbit, Ground Control & Communications, Mission Duration & EOL), conclusion, bibliography. Figures labelled? Images are labelled "STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart", "Sun-Synchronous Circular Orbit, Inclination vs Altitude", "DN path for orbits 1-15", "AN/DN path for orbits 1-15". They are not numbered as Figure 1, Figure 2 etc. Tables have no captions or numbers. The access table has header but no table number/title. The launch tables are raw, no captions. References: bibliography is just URLs, no titles, inconsistent formatting, some entries have stray characters. In-text citations [1]-[10]. Wikipedia used as source [6] "Timeline of spaceflight" - Wikipedia not accepted. This violates R15. Writing: some grammar issues ("an Earth observation satellite", "which is also desirable" typo), but generally readable. Executive summary good. Formatting inconsistent: table formatting broken but likely OCR artifact; but figure numbering absent. References poorly formatted. So C4 Adequate (4-6) or Deficient? It has headings, figures labelled by titles but not numbered; references match in-text but poorly formatted; no figure/table numbers. The rubric Adequate: "Although figures and tables are labelled, the formatting is unclear and/or inconsistent..." That fits. Deficient for unlabelled figures or tables; here figures have descriptive labels but no numbers. Tables are not labelled with numbers/titles (launch tables, access table). That could be deficient. But overall document is readable. I'd say Adequate 5.

Now requirements R1-R15.

R1: Design a space mission that benefits Australia, simple concept. Yes, coral reef monitoring. Met.

R2: Identify and describe main elements of space segment. The report describes satellite, orbit, launch, ground segment. Space segment elements: spacecraft, payload (fluid lensing camera), orbit, power (solar panels). Some description. Met? They mention payload and solar panels, but not detailed subsystem. "Main elements of space segment" could be satisfied by orbit/spacecraft. Partial? They don't describe bus, comms, etc. But requirement is broad. I'd say partial.

R3: State primary mission. Yes, coral reef/ocean monitoring using fluid lensing. Met.

R4: State whether one or multiple spacecraft. Yes, one satellite and why. Met.

R5: Identify users, operator and customers. They identify governmental/science agencies (CSIRO, BOM), funding by university/government. Operator? They say operated and accessed from Australia ground facilities. But not a specific operator. Customers: research/education. Partial? They don't name a specific operator (e.g., CSIRO) and customer. But they mention likely users. I'd say partial.

R6: Specify launch site and launch vehicle. Yes, Guiana Space Centre, Vega E. Met.

R7: Specify orbit type and characteristics and orbital elements. Yes, SSO, COE table. Met.

R8: Identify any orbital manoeuvres. They say only EOL manoeuvre, no others. Met? They don't discuss launch injection manoeuvres. But answer is given. Met.

R9: Identify ground control facilities and state how often communicate. Ground station identified (Mt Pleasant). Frequency: they give access table but not explicit number per day. They say "already frequent amount of passes" and average duration. Could be considered not clearly stated. Partial.

R10: State mission duration and EOL plans. Yes, 5 years, drag sail deorbit. Met.

R11: Complete design using software (STK) and hand calculations. Yes, STK used, hand calc for inclination. Met.

R12: Include relevant screenshots and all relevant STK/PIGI files. Screenshots included. Software files not included in the report (no appendix with files). Deliverable says include files with report or appendix. Not present. Partial.

R13: Single PDF with required sections. It has exec summary, intro, main body, conclusion, bibliography. Met (assuming PDF).

R14: Fully and correctly label all figures and tables (figure number, title, reference). Figures have titles but no numbers. Tables have no numbers/titles. Not fully correct. Partial or no? Many figures have descriptive text but not "Figure 1: ...". Tables not labelled. So partial.

R15: Clearly identify and properly cite all non-original text, no Wikipedia. In-text citations present. Bibliography uses URLs only, some malformed. Wikipedia used as source [6]. This violates "do not use Wikipedia". Also some references lack titles/authors. So partial/no. Since Wikipedia is used, not met fully. Partial.

Technical issues list: 
- RAAN 27.33° claimed to indicate launch facility location - incorrect.
- "very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" - contradictory/typo.
- "constant supply of sunlight" for descending path - SSO still has eclipses; not constantly sunlit.
- Launch vehicle Vega E not yet built; selecting it for 2025 is risky; they acknowledge but still.
- No explicit communication frequency (passes/day).
- No software files included.
- Missing figure/table numbering.
- Wikipedia citation.
- Reference formatting poor.
- Lack of sensor/swath/resolution calculation to justify 600 km.
- "solar panels ... may lengthen lifespan" - odd.
- Access table duplicate row (15 same as 14) maybe OCR artifact? Could be STK duplicate? Not major.
- RAAN initial value 27.33° - arbitrary? They claim indicates launch facility, but launch site longitude is -52.6°, not RAAN. RAAN is defined in inertial frame; launch site location doesn't directly set RAAN. So incorrect.
- Inclination formula: they plotted "mean orbital inclination" vs altitude; value 97.7924° for 600 km seems correct. Good.

Overall: A decent report but with gaps. Need to assign marks.

Let's decide final marks.

C1: Accomplished 8. It addresses all requirements, detailed, references. Users slightly vague but overall high.

C2: Adequate 6. Covers many aspects but missing some details/evidence, technical errors.

C3: Adequate 5. Conclusions present but generic, lack specific quantitative results.

C4: Adequate 5. Structure okay, but figures/tables not numbered, references poor, Wikipedia.

Could C4 be Deficient? The rubric Deficient: "unlabelled figures or tables" - here figures are labelled with descriptive titles but not numbered; tables are not labelled at all (no table captions). That could be considered unlabelled. But the document is readable, headings used. I'd stick with Adequate low 5. However, the references use Wikipedia and are poorly formatted. Still Adequate.

C2 could be 6. If we want Accomplished 7, the missing software files and communication frequency explicit are significant. So 6.

Need to include evidence quotes.

For C1 evidence: Introduction section: "The spacecraft is intended to image and send data to ground stations for collation and analysis." Also "only one satellite is required" and users "governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)". Quote limits <=25 words.

For C2 evidence: "The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport." Also orbit COE table, STK access table.
